scope: Two OpenMS4 benchmark blockers of the mzML reader. (1) Source-compatible reading of a run startTimeStamp or processingMethod completion time that DateTime::set rejects, including the ProteoWizard sentinel "-infinity" and the Boost spellings "infinity" and "not-a-date-time"; selected by mzml::ReadOptions::source_invalid_timestamps (and ReadOptions::source()), with the default staying strict. (2) Size-derived cumulative reader ceilings: every cumulative allowance is floor + per_byte * consumed XML bytes, applied together with the absolute ReadOptions/LoadOptions ceilings, which now default to unbounded. The Numpress coder allowance becomes per array; the scientific selection allowance stays cumulative but scales.

source_anchors.operation: DateTime::set throws Exception::ParseError for text no format matches, the sentinels included; the type has no notion of a sentinel, so the leniency belongs at the mzML boundary

asDateTime_: trims, keeps the first 19 characters, calls DateTime::set, catches ParseError, calls error(LOAD, 'DateTime conversion error of ...') and returns an unset DateTime; an empty string returns unset silently
error(LOAD, msg) prints 'Non-fatal error while loading ...' on OPENMS_LOG_ERROR and returns; loading continues
cvParamToValue, XSD_DATE branch: a value DateTime::set rejects warns and returns DataValue::EMPTY, so handleCVParam_ (MzMLHandler.cpp:1539) returns before the completion time is stored
run: exp_->setDateTime(asDateTime_(start_time)); the raw text is kept as mzml_start_time_stamp only when longer than 19 characters
writer: startTimeStamp is emitted only when the run DateTime is valid, and mzml_start_time_stamp is excluded from the run userParams (line 5229)
contrast for the ceilings: the source reserves from the declared list count and has no resource ceiling of any kind

external_reference_note: No C++ is committed to this repository. The C++ driver is a shell script under ../oracle/mzml-reader-scale/ that runs the prebuilt Release TOPP tools at /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/opt/openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 (BUILD_MANIFEST.json there records the build); only its results enter the repository, as the oracle TSV above. The benchmark inputs stay on /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/bench/openms4/inputs and are read only by #[ignore]d tests.
method: Tier 1: datetime_sentinel_cpp.sh replaced run/@startTimeStamp in a three-spectrum slice of 50amol_R1.mzML with -infinity, infinity, not-a-date-time, an empty value and a valid control, added a processingMethod completion time of not-a-date-time in a sixth case, and ran the C++ Release FileInfo, FileConverter and MzMLSplitter on each. Exit codes, stderr and the written run element are the expected values in tests/mzml_reader_scale.rs. Tier 4: an instrumented reader with every ceiling disabled measured the charge of each cumulative allowance per consumed XML byte on all six benchmark mzML inputs (0.5-2.3 GB, uncompressed and zlib); the InputScaling defaults keep the former fixed ceilings as floors and grant at least eight times the largest measured ratio per byte. The #[ignore]d HPC tests then read every input with the defaults and compare spectrum counts against inputs/MANIFEST.json, which a Python header scan produced. Synthetic documents (20,000 sparse spectra; 4,000 zlib and 6,500 Numpress spectra of 200-500 points) show that the former fixed ceilings, reproduced by InputScaling::fixed, reject a realistic file while the size-derived ones admit it, and adversarial documents (a declared billion points, a 4,000-fold zlib bomb, a 20,000-parameter group expanded per spectrum, 200 levels of nesting) stay refused.
